issues.description: Method singFarmSong(): Problem statement and template expect a void method that prints the song, while the reference solution implements singFarmSong() with return type String and returns the full song text. Specifically: problem_statement.md instructs "Implement the method singFarmSong() inside Farm.java, which prints the ... song" (expects printing/void); template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares public void singFarmSong() and its body contains TODO comments (void/print); solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares public String singFarmSong() and returns the song as a String. This mismatch leaves students uncertain whether to implement printing (void) or returning a String, and causes tests or autograding to fail depending on which behavior is expected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected signature and behavior consistent across all artifacts. Two viable options: (A) Change the problem statement and the template to require public String singFarmSong() that returns the full song (update the description, UML, and template signature/body to build and return the song String) — this makes testing deterministic. Or (B) Change the solution to implement public void singFarmSong() that prints the song directly (update the solution signature and replace the returned String with printing calls). Apply the chosen approach to problem_statement.md, the template Farm.java signature/body, and the UML/description so all three artifacts match.
